description: Collaboration roadmap for SANDWICH v2 — from a messy brief to an execution-ready spec. See [`PRODUCT.md`](./PRODUCT.md) for product intent and [`README.md`](./README.md) for setup.

milestones.name: Project entity & storage foundation
milestones.goal: Introduce a first-class `projects` entity and a persistent per-project directory on disk that becomes the source of truth for every generated artifact. Postgres keeps only an index.

issues.title: Railway Volume provisioning + single-instance constraint
issues.what: Mount a Railway Volume at `/data`, set `PROJECTS_ROOT=/data/projects`, and document that the API service now runs as a single instance (no horizontal scaling) because the volume is single-attach.
issues.why: The filesystem is now canonical for artifacts, so it must survive redeploys. Railway container disk is ephemeral; a Volume is the persistent option.
acceptance: Volume mounted and `PROJECTS_ROOT` set in Railway
Boot check logs a clear fatal error if `PROJECTS_ROOT` is missing or not writable
README.md / PRODUCT.md updated with the single-instance constraint
issues.notes: The existing Redis in-flight coordination stays as a safety net but is no longer load-bearing.

issues.title: Retire `document_versions` / `document_files`; slim `documents` to an index
issues.what: Drop both tables. Reshape `documents` to: id, project_id, conversation_id (nullable — "generated in"), type, title, relative_path, last_commit_sha, timestamps. No migration of existing rows — clean slate.
issues.why: Git in the project directory becomes the version store. Postgres only needs a pointer to the file on disk and the latest commit SHA.
acceptance: Migration drops `document_versions` and `document_files` and alters `documents`
`apps/server/db/documents.ts` rewritten to the new shape
All code paths that read versions/files updated or removed (`prototype/engine.ts`, `prototype/routes.ts`, `routes/documents.ts`, `routes/conversation-run.ts`)
`conversation_documents` removed in favour of `documents.conversation_id`
issues.notes: This is a breaking schema change; coordinate with M2 and M4 so nothing reads the dropped tables after the migration.

milestones.name: Pi SDK on the project workspace
milestones.goal: Every engine runs like Pi / Claude Code in a local checkout: `cwd` is the project directory, context comes from the files there, and output is written back as files.

issues.title: Run all engines with `cwd = project dir` + tools
issues.what: Replace the ephemeral `tmpdir()` workspace (prototype engine) and `process.cwd()` (text engine) with the resolved project directory. Give every engine the tool set read / write / edit / ls / grep / find / bash. Keep the existing timeout guards.
issues.why: Unifies the two engines and lets a later pass (e.g. quotation) read a deliverable the user already generated in the same project — exactly how a local coding agent works.
acceptance: `runTextGeneration` and `generatePrototypeDocument` both take `projectDir` and pass it as `cwd`
Text engine is no longer tool-free
PRODUCT.md §6 ("text engine stays tool-free") updated
issues.notes: Watch for the historical text-engine hangs with tools (PRODUCT.md §6). If they recur, add a tool-call ceiling and/or a stricter timeout rather than reverting.

issues.title: `BRIEF.md` builder
issues.what: Before each run the backend (re)writes `BRIEF.md` at the project root: the consolidated brief, clarifying Q&A, and short summaries of any uploaded attachments. This is the only user-originated context that lands on disk.
issues.why: Gives every engine grounding without dumping raw chat logs or raw uploads into `cwd`, which would be context noise the agent picks up via `ls` / `read`.
acceptance: `BRIEF.md` regenerated on each generate run and committed with that run
Chat transcript, intake, and pipeline/session state stay in Postgres
Raw attachment bytes stay in R2; only extracted-text summaries go into `BRIEF.md`
issues.notes: Replaces the current inline attachment injection (`enrichMessageContent`) for large attachments; small ones can still be inlined into the prompt.

issues.title: Text deliverables written as files in the project
issues.what: PRD / quotation / specs / MOM land as `prd.md`, `quotation.md`, `spec.md`, `mom.md` at the project root, produced by the agent via the `write` tool. The backend records/updates the `documents` index row and commits.
issues.why: "Layaknya codebase" — one file per deliverable, overwrite on regenerate, history in git.
acceptance: Each deliverable type maps to a fixed filename at the project root
Regenerate overwrites the same file (new commit, not a new file)
`documents.relative_path` and `last_commit_sha` updated after each run
issues.notes: One deliverable of each type per project for now.

issues.title: Prototype → single `prototype/index.html`
issues.what: Prototype output becomes a single self-contained `prototype/index.html` inside the project directory. Drop the multi-file save-to-Postgres loop and the tmpdir workspace. Refine edits the file in place.
issues.why: The user wants single-HTML prototypes for now; the multi-file model and its Postgres persistence go away with `document_files`.
acceptance: Prototype run writes/edits only `prototype/index.html`
Refine edits the existing file in place, not a regenerate
Decision recorded on whether the glowup polish pass still runs (in place) or is deferred

issues.title: Persist the Pi session per conversation
issues.what: Swap `SessionManager.inMemory` for a disk-backed session keyed by `conversation_id`, stored OUTSIDE the project directory (e.g. `${PI_SESSIONS_ROOT}/${conversationId}`). One project can have several conversations, hence several sessions, all sharing the same `cwd`.
issues.why: Matches "session per conversation, context from the folder": the agent keeps conversational continuity while the project files are the shared substrate.
acceptance: Session store path is outside `cwd` — no session files pollute the project directory
Resuming a conversation resumes its Pi session
Deleting a conversation removes its session store
issues.notes: Check whether `pi.SessionManager` ships a disk-backed manager; otherwise wrap one.

issues.title: Serialize generation runs per project
issues.what: Extend the in-flight guard from per-conversation to also lock the project directory, so two conversations in the same project cannot run generations concurrently against the same git working tree.
issues.why: Concurrent writes and commits to one git repo corrupt its state.
acceptance: A second concurrent run in the same project queues or is rejected with a clear message
The lock is released on completion, error, and timeout
issues.notes: `inFlight` map in `apps/server/routes/conversation-run.ts` plus the Redis keys in `apps/server/redis.ts`.

milestones.name: Versioning via git
milestones.goal: Replace the Postgres version snapshots with git operations on each project repository.

issues.title: Commit per generation
issues.what: After every successful generate / refine, stage the changed deliverable(s) + `BRIEF.md` and commit with a structured message (deliverable type + version, conversation id, prompt summary). Persist the resulting SHA to `documents.last_commit_sha`.
issues.why: The git log becomes the version history that the sidebar and rollback read from.
acceptance: Exactly one commit per successful run, app-authored, with metadata in the body
`last_commit_sha` updated on the affected `documents` rows
An empty diff produces no commit and a "nothing changed" reply
issues.notes: Commit via `child_process` inside the workspace module from M1-03.

issues.title: Rollback via git
issues.what: Rewire the existing rollback-intent parsing (`apps/server/prototype/rollback.ts`) to git: "rollback ke v2" resolves the Nth deliverable commit and restores that file, then commits the restore.
issues.why: The rollback UX already exists in chat; only the backing store changes.
acceptance: "rollback", "kembali ke versi sebelumnya", "v2" all resolve to git operations
Rollback creates a new commit — no history rewrite
Preview reflects the rolled-back file
issues.notes: Operate per deliverable file, not the whole tree.

issues.title: Version history + diff API
issues.what: Endpoints that return the `git log` for a deliverable (SHA, date, message, prompt summary) and a unified diff between two SHAs, for the sidebar version panel.
issues.why: PRODUCT.md §7 promises version history and per-prompt diffs in the sidebar.
acceptance: `GET /api/projects/:id/documents/:type/history`
`GET /api/projects/:id/documents/:type/diff?from=&to=` returns unified diff text
Both guarded by project ownership

milestones.name: Preview & retrieval from the filesystem
milestones.goal: Serve prototype previews and document content from disk (and from past commits) instead of Postgres.

issues.title: `/p` preview served from disk
issues.what: `/p/:projectId/` serves `prototype/index.html` from the project directory; `/p/:projectId/v/:sha/` serves that file at a past commit via `git show`. Keep the auth check.
issues.why: `document_files` is gone; the preview must read the on-disk file.
acceptance: Latest and versioned preview both work from disk
404 when no prototype file exists for the project
`prototypePreviewUrl` updated from `/p/:docId` to `/p/:projectId`

issues.title: Document read / download from disk
issues.what: Document content endpoints in `apps/server/routes/documents.ts` read the file from the project directory (optionally at a given SHA) instead of `document_versions`.
issues.why: Same reason — the version tables no longer exist.
acceptance: Get latest content, get content at a SHA, and download (.md / .html) all work
Every read goes through `resolveInsideProject`

issues.title: Project file-tree API for the sidebar
issues.what: `GET /api/projects/:id/files` returns the deliverables present on disk (type, filename, last commit, updated-at) to power the document panel.
issues.why: The sidebar now reflects a directory, not a set of `documents` rows with embedded content.
acceptance: Lists the known deliverables that exist on disk
`BRIEF.md`, `.git`, and any internal files are excluded or flagged internal

milestones.name: Durability & lifecycle
milestones.goal: Back the single-copy volume with R2, and handle project deletion and storage limits.

issues.title: R2 backup per project
issues.what: After each commit, asynchronously push a `git bundle` of the project repo to R2 under `projects/:userId/:projectId.bundle`.
issues.why: The Railway Volume is a single copy. R2 is the durability net and the escape hatch if we later change hosts or need to scale out.
acceptance: Bundle uploaded after each commit, non-blocking, retried on failure
Backup failures are logged and surfaced in metrics, never to the user

issues.title: Lazy-restore a project from R2
issues.what: When a project directory is requested but missing on disk (volume recreated, new host), restore it from its R2 bundle before use.
issues.why: Makes the volume disposable and keeps redeploys safe even if the volume is wiped.
acceptance: Missing dir + existing bundle → cloned from the bundle transparently
Missing dir + no bundle → treated as a new empty project
Restore is idempotent and locked per project

issues.title: Project deletion
issues.what: Deleting a project removes its DB rows (conversations, documents, chat_messages, attachment metadata), its on-disk directory, its R2 bundle, and its R2 attachment objects. Deleting a single conversation removes only that conversation + its Pi session, never the project.
issues.why: No orphaned disk or object storage.
acceptance: DB rows removed in one transaction; disk + R2 cleanup best-effort with logging
Deleting a conversation leaves the project and its other conversations intact

issues.title: Per-user disk guardrails
issues.what: Cap total project bytes per user (and per project), with a clear error when exceeded. Keep the existing monthly document / chat quotas.
issues.why: Filesystem storage per user is now effectively unbounded.
acceptance: Size check before a generate run writes files
Limits configurable per plan (Starter vs Pro)
Over-limit returns 403 with an actionable message
